A_target.statement:
In a [[Definition:Hilbert Proof System|Hilbert system]] for propositional logic with [[Definition:Modus Ponendo Ponens|modus ponens]] and the axiom schemes:
:$\phi \to \paren {\psi \to \phi}$
:$\paren {\phi \to \paren {\psi \to \chi} } \to \paren {\paren {\phi \to \psi} \to \paren {\phi \to \chi} }$
if $\Gamma \cup \set \phi \vdash \psi$ then $\Gamma \vdash \phi \to \psi$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\map P \phi$ be a property of [[Definition:Well-Formed Formula|formulas]].
If $\map P \phi$ holds for atomic formulas and is preserved by each formation rule, then $\map P \phi$ holds for every formula.

derived.the inductive property: Gamma proves phi -> psi_i for each line psi_i

object_map.reformulation: Reuse the induction-over-construction plan, now over the lines of a derivation, with one case per way a line can be justified.

validity_conditions: The two axiom schemes are exactly what is needed for the hypothesis case and the modus ponens case.
The derivation is finite, so induction on its length applies.
proof_plan:
Let $\psi_1, \ldots, \psi_n = \psi$ be a derivation from $\Gamma \cup \set \phi$.
Show by induction on $i$ that $\Gamma \vdash \phi \to \psi_i$.

If $\psi_i$ is an axiom or lies in $\Gamma$, then from $\psi_i$ and $\psi_i \to \paren {\phi \to \psi_i}$, modus ponens gives $\phi \to \psi_i$.
If $\psi_i = \phi$, then $\vdash \phi \to \phi$ follows from the two schemes.

If $\psi_i$ follows by modus ponens from $\psi_j$ and $\psi_j \to \psi_i$, the induction hypothesis gives $\Gamma \vdash \phi \to \psi_j$ and $\Gamma \vdash \phi \to \paren {\psi_j \to \psi_i}$.
The second scheme and two applications of modus ponens give $\Gamma \vdash \phi \to \psi_i$.

Taking $i = n$ gives $\Gamma \vdash \phi \to \psi$, which is the [[Deduction Theorem]].
{{qed}}
